verdicts.trueWording: "when Brenda sounded odd and graceless, people were less likely to get intimate, which meant less HUMAN_FALLBACK"
verdicts.note: Raw n+1 page fetched (HTTP 200, browser UA). Quote exact in the paragraph beginning "Eventually I reached a level of virtuosity". The escalation limb is supported: the essay defines HUMAN_FALLBACK as Brenda's "white flag of surrender" with which "Brenda ceded the conversation to me" (the human operator), so "less HUMAN_FALLBACK" = fewer conversations escalated to a human.

verdicts.trueWording: "In many cases, these works have been “co-written” with “AI” or simply given a polishing edit in an attempt to make them less obvious... they still display the hallmarks I’ve come to expect"
verdicts.note: Raw Clarkesworld Aug 2025 editorial fetched (HTTP 200). Quote exact; both limbs (co-written / polishing edit to disguise, and hallmarks he has come to expect) present in the same sentence pair.

verdicts.trueWording: "Given that I’ve seen some flash and poetry examples of these works find publication elsewhere (the tells are more obvious on longer works)"
verdicts.note: Quote exact and genuinely parenthetical. The causal "which is why" is carried by the parenthesis's placement immediately after the flash/poetry-publication clause, which is its plain function; both facts are stated on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: "co-writing with something that has produced some of the worst stories I’ve read"
verdicts.note: Quote exact, in the paragraph beginning "If any of that makes you nervous". Page uses the singular "something" (the AI system) rather than plural "systems"; substance identical.

verdicts.trueWording: "At its peak, our submissions more than doubled due to the high volume of generated works."
verdicts.note: Quote exact, in the paragraph beginning "The good news is that the adaptations we made to our submissions process". Peak-of-surge limb explicit ("At its peak").

verdicts.trueWording: "The number of false positives and negatives was simply unacceptable and I observed an even greater error rate when it came to works written by non-native English speakers"
verdicts.note: Quote exact, in the paragraph beginning "I was already thinking ahead to this scenario". The evaluation limb is supported both by that paragraph's subject (commercial detection tools/"their products") and by his later statement "I’ve been regularly evaluating these products since 2023".

verdicts.trueWording: "I would never trust an algorithm to make a final assessment... As such, I personally evaluate each suspicious submission."
verdicts.note: Raw neil-clarke.com post (dated 05/02/2025) fetched (HTTP 200). Quote exact, in the paragraph beginning "No process is perfect"; the automated check is the post's "oval" in-house automated step that routes “suspicious” submissions to a separate queue.

verdicts.trueWording: "even if we set aside our legal and ethical concerns with how these systems were developed, the output of these tools is nowhere near the standards we expect"
verdicts.note: Quote exact, in the closing section paragraph beginning "And repeated from the previous post". Both limbs (setting aside legal and ethical concerns; nowhere near Clarkesworld's standards) present verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: "This, I claim, is the main stylistic hallmark of both R1 and the new OpenAI model" ... "one thing that is abstract and/or incorporeal" / "another thing that is concrete and/or sensory"
verdicts.note: Raw Tumblr page fetched (HTTP 200, browser UA; full post body present, not a shell). Quote exact in section "A mechanical boot, a human eye". The OpenAI model is described earlier as "the new, unreleased OpenAI model".

verdicts.trueWording: "R1 even consistently does this in spite of user-specified stylistic directions. To wit: when I tried prompting R1 to mimic the styles of a bunch of famous literary authors..."
verdicts.note: Quote exact in "A mechanical boot, a human eye". The named-author limb is the following sentence: mimicking "famous literary authors" yielded the eyeball kicks "in virtually every case".

verdicts.trueWording: "(The one exception being the Hemingway pastiche, presumably because Hemingway himself has a distinctive and constrained style which leaves no room for these kinds of flourishes.)"
verdicts.note: Quote exact; it is the parenthesis immediately after the pastiche discussion, exactly as the page hint says. Both limbs (sole exception; attributed to Hemingway's constrained style) present.

verdicts.trueWording: "There’s no modulation, no room to breathe – just an unrelenting stream of “gee-whiz” effects."
verdicts.note: Quote exact in "A mechanical boot, a human eye"; the referent "This kind of prose" is the "crammed prose full of eyeball kicks" named two paragraphs above, so the "crammed prose" limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: "I would guess it’s convergent evolution: maybe this is just what happens if you optimize for human judgments of “literary quality” in some fairly generic, obvious, “naive” manner"

verdicts.trueWording: "In the hands of humans, these are techniques that can be deployed to specific ends; the LLMs seem to use them arbitrarily and incessantly"

verdicts.trueWording: "First: personification of nature (or the inanimate)... possibly because it’s a fairly easy technique... which nonetheless strikes most people as distinctively “literary”"
